title: OBS Studio homepage
firstScreenJob: Confirm the tool, expose platform downloads, and explain the core streaming promise fast.

traversal: Traversal is strongly sequential: hero proof first, then a numbered scroll story with chapter links like 1.0 Intake through 5.0 Monitor that progressively widen the product scope.
responsiveBehavior: The fetched page is presented as a single-column narrative with nav, hero simulation, and stacked chapter sections; exact breakpoint swaps or mobile-only controls were not directly observable.
motion: The text capture exposed static image placeholders and no inspectable timing data; any animation in the live product frames was not directly observable here.
visualWorld: Editorial software showcase with dense in-product snapshots, numbered chaptering, restrained chrome, and a strong sense of operational realism built from issue text, agents, diffs, and dashboards.
strengths: The hero demonstrates the product in context instead of opening with abstract brand copy.
Numbered chapter structure gives the long page a memorable narrative spine.
The simulated data is specific enough to make the product feel operational rather than conceptual.
weaknesses: The first screen is cognitively heavy and may overwhelm visitors who do not already understand the category.
Headline repetition in the fetched output weakens crispness at the top of the page.
The homepage commits hard to one dense product-story mode rather than offering a lighter skim path early.
transferableDecisions: Use one believable scenario with domain-specific data to establish credibility immediately.
Organize long homepages as explicit chapters when the product spans multiple jobs.
Let proof modules show artifacts, actor names, and state changes instead of relying on generic feature cards.
